{{short description|Reference point in statistics}}
In statistics, an '''inherent zero''' is a reference point used to describe data sets which are indicative of magnitude of an absolute or relative nature. Inherent zeros are used in the [[Level of measurement#Ratio scale|"ratio level" of "levels of measurement"]] and imply "none".<ref>Elementary Statistics: Picturing the World by [[Ron Larson (mathematician)|Ron Larson]] and Elizabeth Farber</ref>
